gaps.sentence: I ___ from Tom since March, which is starting to worry me.
gaps.hint: since March continuing into the present
gaps.explanation: 'Since March' up to now takes the present perfect: haven't heard.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: This perfume ___ of roses and vanilla.
gaps.hint: perceived smell is a state verb
gaps.explanation: Verbs of perception like 'smell' are state verbs, so the present simple is used: smells.

gaps.sentence: Look — someone ___ that vase; it is in pieces on the floor.
gaps.hint: look plus a visible present result
gaps.explanation: The present result of a very recent action takes the present perfect: has broken.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ at six tomorrow morning, as it does every day.
gaps.explanation: Timetabled events use the present simple.

gaps.sentence: I ___ what the problem is, so let me explain it to the others.
gaps.hint: see meaning understand is a state
gaps.explanation: When 'see' means 'understand', it is a state verb and cannot be continuous: see.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the car tonight, so take a taxi into town.
gaps.hint: a future activity in progress as reason
gaps.explanation: The future continuous can express something in progress around a future time, here as a polite reason: will be using.

gaps.sentence: They ___ for two hours when the storm hit.
gaps.hint: two hours of walking before the storm
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous: had been walking.
